- Overestimate prices when sentiment is low or neutral (especially near 0.00–0.18), as models tend to ignore bearish signals.
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes (e.g., >75.00) — models overshoot and fail to correct downward momentum.
- Overreact to recent sentiment peaks — if sentiment rises sharply, model overweights it and forecasts higher than true mean.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 74.00 for 3+ days, model often overcorrects downward; if below 70.00, it undercorrects upward.
- Forecast horizon 30d: models consistently overpredict early in the window (first 5–7 days) and underpredict late (last 5–7 days), especially when sentiment is weak.
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.20), reduce forecast amplitude by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in upward bias.
- If sentiment is rising from low to medium (0.18–0.44), model often fails to adjust downward — overestimates peak before mean reversion.
- Avoid forecasting spikes >76.00 unless sentiment is >0.36 — models overfit to short-term momentum and ignore long-term mean.
